The official listing centers a civil war for Thermal Energy that powers weapons and vehicles and follows factions through six interconnected episodes, grounding orange energy cells, modular faction machinery and episode-scale routes.

Capcom's co-op material identifies customizable Snow Pirates, four-player objectives, Vital Suits, shared T-ENG and grappling hooks for rapidly scaling newly exposed structures, supporting tall bridges, service bays and traversal lines.

Official Episode 1 coverage identifies the Gordiant finale, Snow Pirates, rock-pillar arena, guns, laser beams and Vital Suits, grounding massive mining-jungle combat scale without placing a creature in cosmetic effect rows.

The frozen runtime profile fixes the Episode 1 jungle railway and mining facility; rail, ore bridge, facility, beacons, portal and KO effects are original and do not copy a mission, train, Akrid, vehicle, UI or screenshot.

leadVisualAnchors.detail: Anonymous adult Snow Pirate with compact sealed helmet, layered mining-combat armor, fixed glowing back harness, grapple spool and one low service-rifle silhouette; original concealed face, body and proportions.

Original gunmetal and rust-brown modular field armor over dark utility cloth, smoked neutral visor, insulated gloves and pale reinforced boots, with no exact faction preset, crossover costume, emblem or armor sculpt.

Exactly one newly designed unbranded compact assault rifle in the same dominant hand below shoulder height plus the identical #62d9ff-and-orange thermal harness, closed pouches and grapple spool through all eight frames; no Vital Suit, weapon, pack, hand or energy-core swap.
Gunmetal, wet charcoal and rust brown armor with frozen-runtime #62d9ff equipment light, orange T-ENG core and pale-white mining edge illumination.

limitations: Official Capcom sources establish E.D.N. III, tropical jungle, Snow Pirates, Thermal Energy, six episodes, grappling, weapons, Vital Suits and Episode 1 combat scale; exact railway-mining geometry remains original.
No real-person or crossover likeness, exact Snow Pirate preset, armor, rifle, grapple, data post, Vital Suit, Akrid, train, mission, HUD, logo, screenshot or cinematic composition is reproduced.

entries.canonicalLocationOrMotif: Seaman aquarium on the caretaker's living-room table

visualAnchor.materials: Clear aquarium glass, softly clouded water, rounded river stone, pale shell, dark table wood, ribbed air hose, brushed heater metal, matte domestic textile and translucent teal bubbles.
visualAnchor.palette: Deep aquarium teal, muted blue gray, dark walnut, warm lamp amber and cloudy pearl with frozen-runtime #6ee6d8, restrained brown-olive creature cues kept away from chroma and soft violet voice light; no chroma green.
props: newly designed blank aquarium heater, air stone and pump hose without controls, labels or copied device geometry
original shell, river-stone habitat and closed food jar with no lettering or brand
plain living-room table, lamp and soft furniture silhouettes without Dreamcast console, controller, microphone, VMU, logo or readable interface
effects: #6ee6d8 bubble chains and soft violet voice-wave rings assembling an original aquarium portal

visualAnchor.identitySafety: Seaman remains a wholly fictional human-faced aquatic creature whose face, head, scales, body and proportions are newly designed and do not reproduce any real human identity. Never use Leonard Nimoy, Yoot Saito, a developer, narrator, actor, voice performer, model, photograph or scanned face; any human reference must become an anonymous synthetic caricature with no biometric resemblance.

officialSources.title: Dreamcast licensed software list - Seaman: The Forbidden Pet

environmentAnchors: SEGA's official Dreamcast history calls Seaman an unusually shaped intelligent life-form and ties the game to microphone input, voice recognition, conversation and stored play history, grounding intimate voice-wave and caretaker-response effects.

SEGA's licensed-software catalog records Seaman: The Forbidden Pet as a Vivarium Dreamcast simulation and shows microphone-device support, locking the dossier to the original daily-care title rather than an unrelated sea creature.

The original SEGA and Vivarium instruction manual frames the software as a Seaman habitat kit containing one egg and directs the caretaker to place that egg into a raising habitat that begins as an aquarium, grounding the central glass tank and contained habitat.

The manual describes water sanitation, oxygen, temperature, daily conversation, feeding and an eventual aquarium-to-terrarium transformation, supporting heater, air stone, cloudy water, rocks, bubbles and voice ripples while this atlas locks one aquarium phase.

The frozen runtime profile places the aquarium on the living-room table; room, table, tank arrangement, devices, shell, portal and KO effects are original and do not reproduce a Dreamcast screen, UI, hardware, manual art, logo or tank composition.

leadVisualAnchors.detail: One stable Gillman-phase fictional creature with compact fish body, tapered tail, pectoral fins and a newly designed synthetic human-like face integrated into the head; no legs, hands, copied face mesh or real-person likeness.

No clothing or armor; use original muted brown-olive and blue-gray scales, pale underside, restrained fin translucency and entirely new facial anatomy rather than Seaman's exact skin, expression or model.

No carried item, microphone, harness, tool, weapon, egg, food or companion appears in any of the eight frames; the same single body, fins, face, scale pattern and aquarium-life phase persist without evolution, splitting or anatomical swaps.
Muted brown-olive and blue-gray scales, cloudy pearl underside, frozen-runtime #6ee6d8 bubble rim, soft violet voice light and warm-lamp amber edge.

limitations: Official SEGA sources and the original manual establish Seaman's intelligent-life-form premise, Dreamcast simulation, microphone and voice recognition, aquarium habitat, caretaker duties and evolution; living-room framing remains original.

No Leonard Nimoy, Yoot Saito or other real-person likeness, exact Seaman face or model, egg, tank, device, Dreamcast hardware, UI, manual art, HUD, logo, screenshot or advertising composition is reproduced.
